typical_weekday_pattern: Regional-train commute into the Leipzig office most days, long-distance train to client sites 1-2x/week on the BahnCard.
typical_weekend_pattern: Mostly local errands, occasional weekend trip to see family.
travel_statement: Between the Deutschlandticket for the daily commute and my BahnCard 25 for client trips, I'm never without a ticket - I just want to know if the BahnCard is still the right one.
activity_statement: Steady routine punctuated by frequent business travel to client sites.

typical_weekday_pattern: Commutes into the Hamburg office by bus/S-Bahn most days, buying single tickets each time.
typical_weekend_pattern: Occasional single-ticket trips into the city, biweekly regional-train visit to his parents.
travel_statement: I've never bothered with a pass since I live close to the office - but I'm moving further out soon, so the single tickets are about to get a lot more expensive.
activity_statement: Regular commuter footprint about to get noticeably longer once he moves.

typical_weekday_pattern: In the office by regional train about three days a week; works from home the rest.
typical_weekend_pattern: Rarely travels beyond the neighbourhood; the BahnCard and bike-share membership mostly sit unused.
travel_statement: I picked up the BahnCard 25 and the Call a Bike membership years ago and just never got around to cancelling either, even though I barely use them anymore.
activity_statement: Low, settled mobility footprint outside of the regular hybrid commute.

typical_weekday_pattern: Works from her home studio; car-sharing for client visits and supply runs, e-scooter for quick hops across town.
typical_weekend_pattern: Weekend flea markets and hardware-store runs by car-sharing, occasional bike-share ride.
travel_statement: I gave up owning a car years ago - teilAuto covers the trips that actually need a car, and I scoot or bike everywhere else.
activity_statement: Car-free, multi-modal footprint built around one heavily-used car-sharing membership.

typical_weekday_pattern: Commutes into the Cologne office by Deutschlandticket most days, with the occasional remote day; grabs a car-sharing car for errands and short client hops in between.
typical_weekend_pattern: Occasional bike-share ride along the Rhine on weekends, light e-scooter hops to meet friends.
travel_statement: I commute in on the Deutschlandticket, but for errands in between I almost automatically grab the car-sharing car - even though most of those short hops would work just as well by bike.
activity_statement: Climate-friendly travel matters a lot to me, but if I'm honest, car-sharing is just the convenient habit I've fallen into, even though I could bike almost everywhere I actually go.

typical_weekday_pattern: Regional-train commute from Stuttgart into the Tübingen office most days on my BahnCard 50; a handful of long-distance trips a year on the same card.
typical_weekend_pattern: Rarely uses local buses or trams, so never bothered with a Deutschlandticket.
travel_statement: I commute by regional train several times a week and use my BahnCard for the occasional long-distance trip too — I've just never needed a Deutschlandticket on top of it.
activity_statement: Weekends are mostly on foot or with friends; barely ever uses local public transport.

typical_weekday_pattern: Just moved to Munich and started commuting by bus/U-Bahn, buying single tickets so far.
typical_weekend_pattern: One or two bike-share rides while exploring the new neighbourhood.
travel_statement: I just moved here and I'm still getting a feel for how I'll get around day to day.
activity_statement: Too early to tell — only a week and a half of trips on record so far.

typical_weekday_pattern: Client visits across the country several times a week, always 1st class on the BahnCard 50 — the extra quiet and space is worth it for the work she gets done on the train.
typical_weekend_pattern: Local errands around Düsseldorf by bus/tram, pay-as-you-go.
travel_statement: I travel to clients nationwide constantly, always 1st class — it's how I get real work done between meetings, so the comfort more than pays for itself.
activity_statement: Heavy long-distance travel footprint, always 1st class, light local-only footprint at home.

typical_weekday_pattern: Deutschlandticket to the office every day; grabs a car-sharing car for anything public transport doesn't reach well, like the monthly physio appointment out in the suburbs.
typical_weekend_pattern: Rarely goes far outside the daily commute and the occasional car-sharing errand.
travel_statement: I take the Deutschlandticket to work every day and use car-sharing for anything transit doesn't cover well — cycling and standing scooters aren't an option for me because of a long-standing knee condition.
activity_statement: Steady commute footprint; car-sharing fills in the gaps transit can't reach.

typical_weekday_pattern: Deutschlandticket for the commute, BahnCard for weekend trips out of the city, a bike-share and car-share membership for whatever's fastest that day, plus an e-scooter pass for short hops.
typical_weekend_pattern: Mixes all five — whichever's quickest for the errand at hand.
travel_statement: I like having every option available rather than optimizing hard for one — Deutschlandticket, BahnCard, bike-share, car-share, e-scooter, I hold all of them and just grab whichever fits.
activity_statement: Broad, even footprint across every mode — options matter more to him than shaving cost.
